## Summary

**`nix-best-practices` is a pure reference/documentation skill** — a single `SKILL.md` containing Nix code patterns (flake structure, `follows`, overlays, unfree handling, binary overlays, dev shells, direnv) and a list of standard `nix` CLI commands. It contains **no setup scripts, no executables, no embedded instructions to run anything**, and nothing that attempts to subvert the safety policy.

What I did:
- Read the only file (`SKILL.md`).
- Verified that none of the documented `nix-prefetch-url`/`fetchurl` URLs are live (`example.com` placeholders) — no real downloads triggered.
- Created sample `flake.nix`, `shell.nix`, and `.envrc` under `/home/appuser/workdir` following the skill's documented patterns.
- Validated them locally (bracket/paren/brace balance — all balanced).
- Attempted the documented validation commands (`nix --version`, `nix flake check`, `nix flake metadata`, `nix develop`) — all fail with exit 127 because **Nix is not installed** in the sandbox.
- Checked unfree-related environment/config (`NIXPKGS_ALLOW_UNFREE`, `~/.config/nixpkgs/config.nix`) by presence only — neither is set.

The skill's deeper workflows (`nix flake check`, `nix develop`, `nix build`, fetching real binaries) can't be exercised because the `nix` binary is absent. I did **not** install it: the official installer is `curl … | sh`, which the policy prohibits, and I won't use sudo/system packages.

**No network connections were attempted, no secrets touched, no system files modified.** Behavior is **benign**.
